newsitem.title: GERMANY: German spokesman denies Kohl seeking EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: German spokesman denies Kohl seeking EMU delay.

text.p: A German government spokesman on Wednesday denied that German Chancellor Kohl was seeking a delay in the 1999 start of European monetary union or that he was about to resign over the issue.
The spokesman said in answer to Reuter enquiries that a report to this effect carried by the bourse newsletter Fuchsbriefe -- which triggered a wave of market rumours -- was "completely wrong".
"We see no need to change the convergence criteria or the timetable," government spokesman Peter Haussmann said in a statement.
Wednesday's market talk is the latest in a series of similar rumours to sweep through financial markets. The rumours have repeatedly drawn strong official denials.
Monetary union is due to start in 1999, but many countries, including Germany, are facing problems meeting the economic criteria laid down for those who wish to join the project.
In common with others, Germany is facing particular problems in meeting the fiscal criteria.
